title: Your feedback was brilliant! A lot of it has been implemented.
author: EldrichArchive
selftext:
I recently shared a first video of an anti-gravity racer inspired by Screamer (1995) and Wipeout. There was a lot of positive response and also quite a bit of feedback, which really motivated me and led to some good improvements. Particularly in terms of the sound, the vehicles’ appearance, the physics of the vehicles and a few other areas.

The game now has a name: UltraLev 3D. And a few people have even offered to help out, including a sound designer who has worked on several well-known video games.

Thank you all! I’ve rarely seen such a positive and productive community.

comments.author: Kindly-Sail6260
comments.body: Looks good but the boost panels directional arrows look backwards? Not sure if that’s a design choice. Also the camera has some jittering when moving your car. For something that fast, I’d find out how other racing games get a smoother result when moving.

replies.author: EldrichArchive
replies.body: LOL. You're the first one to notice the arrows. Yeah, it was actually a deliberate choice, because the < was meant to suggest “filling up” ...  But I see why that could be confusing. The “jittering” has actually already been fixed, but it hasn't been implemented in this current third-person perspective yet. I'm currently testing different variants ... some more dynamic, some more fixed.

comments.author: Schnitzhole
comments.body:
You might be able to pull some inspiration from the recently killed off [r/rocketracing](r/rocketracing)

Looks cool though. I think you could work on making the impacts with other vehicles feel more punchy instead of carboard boxes colliding or moving over eachother. Like maybe they can actually jump over eachother on purpose or something too.

Any reason the tracks dont turn faster? cause it looks like you could just take the fast inside lane everywhere. Try to have more technical turns and have the track split off side by side or over and under to give it some unique replay ability. The jumps also looked like forced forward warps which removes the suspense of possibly falling from the look of it.
